newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Robotics profits jump 77 percent.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Robotics profits jump 77 percent.

text.p: U.S. Robotics reported a surprisingly strong 77 percent jump in fiscal second-quarter profits Wednesday, citing strong demand for its products, especially its new, speedy x2 modems.
The world's largest consumer modem maker posted net income of $91.5 million, or 95 cents a share, for the quarter ended March 31 vs. $51.6 million, or 55 cents a share in the first quarter of 1996.
The latest results included a tax benefit of $17.9 million, or 18 cents a share, from U.S. Robotics' acquisition of Scorpio Communications Inc.
Sales totalled $690.1 million, up 52 percent from last year's $454.5 million, the Skokie, Ill.-based company said.

U.S. Robotics pointed to strong demand for the x2 modems, which allow Internet connections at speeds up to 56 kilobits per second, about twice as fast as today's standard modems, over conventional phone lines.
U.S. Robotics began shipping its x2 desktop computer modems in February and x2 technology for the hubs used by online services in March.
Chief Operating Officer John McCartney said demand remained strong for modems and hubs, used by online service providers, as well as its personal computer cards and PalmPilot hand-held organisers.
McCartney added he expects demand for all U.S. Robotics' product lines to grow during the rest of the company's fiscal year, as worldwide requirements for information access products increases.

U.S. Robotics said it expects to complete its merger with 3Com Corp. in June and does not expect to report separate results for the June quarter. In February, 3Com agreed to acquire U.S. Robotics for 1.75 3Com shares per U.S. Robotics share.
